subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: India's National Emblem, showing four lions standing back to back, is adapted from the Lion Capital erected by Emperor Ashoka at:
explanation: The National Emblem is adapted from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath (where Buddha gave his first sermon), adopted as the official emblem in 1950 — the accompanying motto 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs) is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.
